findings.summary: The caption states 'the nova axis and X-point are drawn', but the rendered panel: none is drawn. A full-image scan of the blue series (51,102,204) finds exactly two compact glyphs in the whole 1400x720 render: the axis triangle, 9x9 px at rows 233-241 and columns 660-668, and a small closed contour loop, 15x11 px at rows 238-251 and columns 635-645. No blue X-point cross of the kind the same style draws in the two TCV panels (10x10 px, 80 ink pixels) appears anywhere, including at the stored-state cross (rows 601-616, columns 626-641), where a reader who has read the caption will look. The panel therefore reads as a solve with no saddle at all, or as one whose saddle coincides with the stored one, when the receiver says neither: the arm's admission record marks it diverted. The mechanism is visible in the drawing path: draw_nulls drops an X-point that falls outside the wall and reports the drop only in a tally return that panels.py discards, while panels.py marks the nova nulls 'drawn' from the field read alone (panels.py:149); a point drawn beyond the axes limits would be invisible for the same reason. Either way, the marker the caption asserts is data the figure does not let a reader see, which holds the node. The fix is to record and surface the null tally and let the caption state what was actually drawn.

The two null-marker pairs of the compared fields are drawn almost on top of each other, so the stored-state glyphs are largely hidden under the nova ones. Measured on the render: the grey axis triangle occupies rows 387-401, columns 693-707 and the blue axis triangle rows 391-398, columns 699-707, inside it; the grey X-point cross occupies rows 547-562, columns 640-647 and the blue cross rows 552-561, columns 643-652, over it. The grey cross carries 60 ink pixels here against 184 in the tightened panel, where it is uncovered, and the grey axis 90 against 127. The coincidence is legible and is itself the panel's message, so the node is not held, but a reader cannot read the stored-state null positions off this panel; a small offset, a hollow inner glyph for the smaller series, or a different shape per series would keep both readable.

All four panels draw a tall, narrow cross-section on the full 1400x720 slide canvas, leaving most of the canvas white: on this panel the plot ink spans columns 603-798 (196 px, 14.0 percent of the canvas width) and rows 104-672 (79.0 percent of the height), and the ITER panels span 282 px (20.1 percent). This is a consequence of equal aspect on a mandated wide canvas rather than decorative ink, so it is recorded rather than held; the reader-facing cost is that at page-column width the 15 grey and 14 blue contours crowd into a few pixels of spacing.

notes: Read-only figure review of the four rendered PNGs named in this review: iter-stored-default-preview.png, iter-stored-tightened-preview.png, tcv-stored-default-preview.png and tcv-stored-tightened-preview.png, each attached both from the reviewed worktree's figures directory and as an image-N.png copy; the pairs were compared and are identical renders. No SVG and no other image was opened, read, listed, searched, rendered or shown, and no file was edited, created, moved, deleted, redrawn, relabelled or reformatted. Crops used to inspect glyphs and wall clipping were written only to this run's scratch directory. Every verdict is anchored in pixels measured from the PNGs (ink bounding boxes, colour census, connected-component glyph inventory) and in the caption, alt text and arm receipts read as text. No caption merely repeats a figure title: each carries both fields' flux ranges, the shared level band, the per-series level counts and the terminal residual and reason, so no caption finding is recorded. The legend's nova entry losing its triangle marker in iter-stored-tightened-preview is consistent with the caption's statement that no blue null is drawn there, and is not recorded as a defect. No suite ran for this figure review; added_failure_count is 0 by construction.
